title: Routing form-driven batch: ISIS/OpenFabric/MPLS and protocol UX cleanup
acceptance_criteria: Routing pages for ISIS, OpenFabric, and MPLS are form-driven with explicit field-level CRUD workflows.
Routing UX no longer falls back to generic in-progress placeholders for unselected states.
Protocol selector pages remove redundant/invalid entries and keep navigation coherent.
Backend app has required service-wrapper modules present for imported routers (dns/lldp/mdns/ntp/ssh).
Typecheck, backend protocol/service tests, build, runtime smoke, and browser smoke pass.
assumptions: This batch focuses on protocol UX depth and stability rather than introducing new protocol families.
Unrelated pre-existing dirty files outside this staged slice remain untouched.
Fixture seeding scripts are for dev validation and not required in production runtime paths.

tasks.notes: Implemented robust form-first routing protocol editors and selector UX refinements.
Added missing wrapper modules required by existing backend imports and service endpoints.
Added protocol seed scripts for deterministic live validation during QA cycles.
Regenerated docs coverage artifacts after routing/service wrapper updates.
Manual review complete for route selection behavior and no-placeholder UX policy.
